scope: Actual Chrome Web Store installation in the existing signed-out Chrome profile against the live server; no source build, unpacked extension, account reset, or usage-policy change

artifact.source: Chrome Extensions details displayed Chrome Web Store
artifact.auth: The side panel displayed the guest banner throughout

sequence_utc.action: In previously used guest profile, open installed Store side panel on the public demo and send a simple arithmetic question
sequence_utc.result: Terminal correct answer; no UI error
Terminal answer recalling the preceding question; no UI error

sequence_utc.action: After closing and reopening the panel in the same installed profile, send Hi in the new conversation
sequence_utc.result: Immediate terminal assistant text: Error: The chat service could not complete this request. Try again. Interruption notice: The response was interrupted by an error. Retry and Dismiss displayed.
sequence_utc.first_failing_boundary: The correlated live POST /v2/ai/mandates/extend.browser_chat returned HTTP 402 in 575 ms at 2026-10-04T05:29:10.852Z

server_correlation.source: Independent live error/usage investigation correlated the above request ID and timestamp
server_correlation.same_guest_usage: Weekly points are over the allowance with enforcement enabled
server_correlation.exact_http_response_body: not retained in the audit log; no claim about its exact JSON shape
server_correlation.request_auth: guest fingerprint, not a signed-in bearer

boundary_diagnosis.confirmed: The installed side panel turns a legitimate guest allowance refusal into a generic retryable chat failure at the client HTTP-error presentation boundary.
boundary_diagnosis.source_contract_gap: src/lib/api/stream.ts isGuestAllowanceUsed recognizes only status 403 with a top-level error field equal to guest_ai_allowance_used, while the live refusal for the reproduced send was status 402. streamErrorMessage has no 402 case and uses generic copy; src/lib/chat/stream-error.ts suppresses Retry only when code is guest_ai_allowance_used.
boundary_diagnosis.qualification: The 0.2.176 Store binary predates this source checkout. The source contract matches the observed generic message and Retry behavior, but exact response-body shape and binary-level branch execution were not captured.

ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.cause: Live allowance HTTP status moved to 402 while the installed client recognizes guest_ai_allowance_used only at 403
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.prediction: A 402 response carrying error=guest_ai_allowance_used yields generic copy and Retry; accepting 402 at the shared classifier yields the free-tries remedy and no Retry
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.test: Run the HTTP-error classifier against the captured 402 status with a representative refusal body, then verify actual Store candidate or newer client against an already-over guest identity
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.state: Strongly supported by live status, UI behavior, and source; exact body still unobserved

ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.cause: The live 402 response body does not contain the field expected by the client
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.prediction: Changing only accepted status leaves the classifier generic; a schema-aware classification test with the actual redacted body identifies the missing field
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.test: Capture one private redacted 402 response shape or inspect the deployed server response constructor without exposing identity
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.state: Open because audit logs do not retain response body

ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.cause: The failure is an unrelated network or session error
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.prediction: The failed send would lack an allowance-gate 402 on the same request ID
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.test: Correlate first failing request status, identity, and usage state
ranked_falsifiable_hypotheses.state: Falsified for this reproduced failure by the correlated 402 and over-allowance guest state

limits: The reporter's exact initial message and profile were not available, so the observed 402 is a faithful installed-surface reproduction of the symptom, not proof of identical user identity.
The earlier two successful turns and the later 402 in the same profile suggest a time-dependent usage/cache boundary; no claim about the cache's internal cause is made here.
No repeated sends were made after the reproduced failure.
